newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - Pollution firms rated, stocks rise.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Pollution firms rated, stocks rise.

text.p: -- Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said it started coverage of the pollution control industry. Two companies that won top 'buy' ratings, Millipore Corp and Australia-based Memtec Ltd, moved higher.
-- In a report, analyst Rod Lache started Memtec and Millipore with buy ratings and Pall Corp with a hold rating.
-- Memtec shares rose three points to 22-1/4.

-- Lache gave Millipore a 12-month price target of $56. "A rebounding semiconductor industry and accelerating demand for pharmaceuticals should propel (Millipore) to 20 perent plus earnings growth over the next two years. We expect long-term growth of 15 to 20 percent," the report said.
-- Millipore shares rose 1-1/8 to 43-5/8 at midday on the New York Stock Exchange. Millipore is the second-largest industrial filtration company in the world after Pall Corp.

-- Lache said Memtec's products and aggressive expansion and acquisition strategy position it to be the fastest-growing filtration company in revenue and earnings. He said its growth opportunities are underappreciated by Wall Street.

"We believe Memetec can sustain 35 percent-plus annual internal earnings per share growth for the next three years ...the stock is trading at only 12.4 times our calendar 1998 (earnings) estimate of $1.55 a share," the report said.
The stock has fallen nearly 40 percent from the beginning of the year after it posted disappointing profits for the second quarter ended December 31.

-- Lache said he expects Pall to return to 15 percent plus earnings growth next year after some temporary factors that have been holding the company's financials recede. He cited a slowdown in the seiconductor industry and blood filtration sales as well as a strong dollar for muted growth at Pall.
-- He said he remained catious on the stock, given uncertainty over its recent purchase of Gelman Sciences and growth in its blood filtration market.
